answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a licensed fossil survey of one named karst ridge. The holder walks that ridge at dusk carrying a lantern, logging each fossil find with an independent paleontologist who catalogues it in a public register. Random spot-checks summon the holder to identify a fossil in place on their own ridge within a day, and one surveyor cannot walk two ridges at once. The survey fee in outside money doubles for each further identity on the same funding trail, so every extra fake costs another real ridge, another season, another human, and twice the prior fee.
